articles.summary: Samsung Heavy Industries Co., Ltd. (SHI), Tesser Atomics (Tesser), the Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department of Ocean Operations and Civil Engineering (NTNU), and DNV, have signed a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU),…
articles.body: MOU Signed to Develop Nuclear-Powered LNG Carrier Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © DNV Samsung Heavy Industries Co., Ltd. (SHI), Tesser Atomics (Tesser), the Norwegian University of Science and Technology Department of Ocean Operations and Civil Engineering (NTNU), and DNV, have signed a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), to cooperate on the development of a nuclear-powered LNG carrier demonstration project. The MOU was signed at a collaborative workshop at DNV’s Høvik headquarters in Norway recently. Under the agreement, the project partners will develop a nuclear-powered LNG carrier vessel concept, designed for operation on a route between LNG terminals in the United States and Europe. The first steps of the project involve the partners working together to set out a roadmap that will outline the concept for the demonstration vessel and a plan for safety assessment and approval, all with a view to realizing a practical commercial pathway for the design, construction, and commissioning of the ship. The vessel concept is built around the integration of Tesser’s marinized fluoride-salt-cooled reactor and will serve as a reference for SFI SAINT - Norway’s nuclear-powered vessel research center. The project will be one of multiple demonstration projects conducted in coordination with the NTNU-led SFI SAINT center. The partners bring a range of expertise and experience to drive the project forward. SHI will lead vessel concept development and marine integration, including shipbuilding feasibility and construction methods. Tesser will lead the reactor technology and nuclear plant development, as well as the reactor-specific safety and licensing work. DNV will contribute its expertise in maritime safety, risk assessment and classification, including hazard identification, a safety assessment framework and a classification and verification roadmap. NTNU will coordinate the research, funding proposals and building the project consortium, support feasibility studies, as well as working on simulations, modeling and testing.

articles.title: Indonesia Approves Plan of Development for Geliga Oilfield Six Months After Discovery
articles.summary: Eni announces that the Indonesian authorities have approved the Plan of Development (POD) for the Geliga field (Ganal PSC), a milestone that advances the development of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place for both fields of Geliga and Gula in…
articles.body: Indonesia Approves Plan of Development for Geliga Oilfield Six Months After Discovery Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 23, 2026 © Eni Eni announces that the Indonesian authorities have approved the Plan of Development (POD) for the Geliga field (Ganal PSC), a milestone that advances the development of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place for both fields of Geliga and Gula in the Kutei Basin and consolidates the company's position as a leading gas producer in Indonesia. The approval, granted just six months after the discovery of Geliga, follows the recent start-up of the Maha project and envisages the development of 5.9 Tcf of gas in place and 250 million barrels of associated condensate from the Geliga discovery, together with 2.2 Tcf of gas in place from the existing Gula discovery, for a total of an estimated 8 Tcf of gas in place. Production from the Geliga/Gula hub is expected to peak at 1 Bcf/d of gas and 50,000 barrels of condensate per day. The integrated development of the two fields will create a third production hub in the Kutei Basin, alongside the producing South Hub and the upcoming North Hub, which is currently under execution following the final investment decision (FID) announced earlier this year. With three production hubs in the Kutei Basin, Eni is set to achieve gross production of approximately 3 Bcf/d of gas and 140,000 barrels of condensate per day in East Kalimantan by the end of the decade. This production will serve both domestic and international markets, leveraging synergies with existing facilities in the area, including the Bontang LNG plant and the Jangkrik Floating Production Unit (FPU). The approval of the POD for the Geliga field—now operated by Searah, the independent upstream energy company established through the strategic partnership between Eni and PETRONAS—marks another milestone in the development of Eni's activities in Indonesia's Kutei Basin. The development will comprise 15 subsea wells, flowlines and a newly built FPSO with a processing capacity of approximately 1 Bcf/d of gas and 80,000 barrels of condensate per day, as well as storage capacity of 1,4 million barrels. Gas will be treated onboard the FPSO and transported via pipeline to the onshore receiving facilities at the Santan Terminal and the East Kalimantan gas network. A portion of the gas will be liquefied at the Bontang LNG facility, while the remainder will be supplied to the domestic market through the pipeline network. Condensate will be stabilized and stored onboard the FPSO before being offloaded to shuttle tankers. This new development, together with the ongoing North Hub and Gendalo-Gandang projects, stems from the close strategic partnership with SKK Migas. These projects will have a positive impact on local content development, further increase utilization of the available capacity at the Bontang LNG plant, and provide additional gas supplies for domestic consumption. The new Geliga hub will benefit from synergies with the ongoing execution of the North Hub project, which is expected to start up in 2028. These synergies will contribute to optimizing both costs and execution timelines for the Geliga/Gula development. Eni directly operates the Peri-Mahakam PSC, the Makassar Strait PSC and the recently awarded Sapukala Block. In October 2026, Eni also signed two binding agreements to sell interests in selected Indonesian upstream assets operated by Searah to Pertamina and Medco.

articles.summary: French authorities are preparing a complex towing operation to free the Malta-flagged bulk carrier MIRO G, which remains stranded on a beach along France’s Atlantic coast after running aground during...
articles.body: Advertise Forum Jobs Subscribe Grab a Seat at the Captain’s Table Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe. Join the leading maritime news network Photo: French Atlantic Maritime Prefecture French authorities are preparing a complex towing operation to free the Malta-flagged bulk carrier MIRO G, which remains stranded on a beach along France’s Atlantic coast after running aground during severe weather last week. In an update Monday, the Atlantic Maritime Prefecture said salvage teams had spent the weekend completing technical assessments and assembling equipment needed for a refloating attempt near Cap de l’Homy, in the Landes department of southwestern France. Central to the operation is a 1,900-meter (6,234-foot) towline being prepared aboard the French emergency towing vessel Abeille Bretagne. The line, transported from the port of La Pallice near La Rochelle, consists of connectable 250-meter sections made from high-strength synthetic fiber. The material is lightweight, buoyant and stronger than steel on an equivalent-weight basis, according to the maritime prefecture. Before attempting to pull the vessel free, salvage teams must restore its ballast pumping capability to remove water and reduce its draft. The work is intended to lighten the ship and improve its chances of being refloated without causing additional damage. Authorities are also watching an improving tidal window. Rising tidal coefficients are expected to provide more than one meter of additional water at high tide compared with conditions on November 19, when the grounding sequence began. The favorable tidal trend is expected to continue through Thursday, November 26. Wind and sea conditions are also improving, although authorities cautioned that conditions remain far from ideal and further strong winds are forecast in the coming days. The MIRO G ran aground during the night of November 19–20 after encountering strong winds and heavy seas off Lit-et-Mixe. The ship had initially anchored approximately three nautical miles offshore before being driven toward the coast. The grounding prompted a coordinated maritime emergency response involving French and Spanish authorities, including deployment of the Spanish salvage tug Sar Gavia and the French tug Abeille Bretagne. Personnel aboard the vessel were subsequently evacuated by helicopter. On Friday, November 20, the French maritime prefect ordered the shipowner to take all necessary measures to arrange the vessel’s refloating as quickly as possible, while ensuring the safety of personnel and protection of the marine environment. Authorities are also preparing pollution-response resources on land and at sea as a precaution against a potential release of fuel or other pollutants during the operation. Despite the improving conditions, officials warned that the longer the ship remains grounded, the greater the risk it will settle deeper into the sand. Even if the initial towing attempt succeeds, an offshore sandbank could create another obstacle as the vessel is moved toward deeper water. The maritime prefecture emphasized that no attempt will proceed until the necessary technical preparations are complete and weather and sea conditions are suitable. The operation remains without a confirmed start date, with authorities seeking to balance the urgency of freeing the vessel against the risks of undertaking a difficult salvage operation in unfavorable conditions. articles.title: $4.4 billion play for ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian oil & gas assets and UK infrastructure expands Vår Energi’s North Sea footprint
articles.summary: Vår Energi is acquiring ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure, strengthening its position as 'Europe’s largest independent E&P company.'
articles.body: Business & Finance November 23, 2026 · 1 hour ago $4.4 billion play for ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian oil & gas assets and UK infrastructure expands Vår Energi’s North Sea footprint Vår Energi is acquiring ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure, strengthening its position as 'Europe’s largest independent E&P company.' MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 3 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea Source: Vår Energi Norway’s oil and gas company Vår Energi has struck a deal to buy ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian upstream business and related infrastructure interests in the United Kingdom (UK) for an enterprise value of $4.425 billion, in a major deal that will strengthen its position in the North Sea and raise its long-term production target to more than 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (boe/d) into the mid-2030s. This acquisition, which includes interests in 13 producing fields, operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area (GEA) and associated export infrastructure, and the Teesside terminal in the UK, is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027 and projected to generate $700 million to $1 billion in post-tax synergies. Together with the previously announced BlueNord combination, the company expects the transaction to further strengthen its position as Europe's largest independent E&P company, positioning it as one of the top three global independent offshore oil and gas producers. Related Articles Fossil Energy Vår Energi-BlueNord merger forging Europe’s new independent oil & gas producer 5 min read The agreed enterprise value of $4.425 billion is based on an economic date of January 1, 2026, while the consideration payable at completion is estimated at around $2.5 billion, net of cash, including cash flow generated by the acquired business from the economic date to completion, as well as customary completion adjustments. The acquisition, expected to close around the end of the first quarter of 2027, is subject to customary conditions, including relevant regulatory and governmental approvals. Vår Energi is also establishing a commodity hedging program for transaction volumes from 2027 through Q1 2028. The firm has secured downside protection for approximately 80% of the additional gas volumes at around $110 per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) while retaining exposure to gas price upside. The acquisition increases the Norwegian player’s long-term production target to above 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day into the mid-2030s. " This is another important step in Vår Energi's growth journey and further strengthens our position on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS). The transaction adds significant scale, reserves and operatorship, while creating the opportunity to unlock materially greater value from a high-quality asset base with substantial remaining resources and development potential. We see significant long-term potential on the NCS. Through the transaction we will continue building on our strong track record of extending the lifetime of fields, which might otherwise have remained underdeveloped. This will contribute to increasing competitiveness and longevity across the NCS, creating further opportunities for industrial development and value creation for all stakeholders and the Norwegian society. " — Nick Walker Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Vår Energi The company will maintain a balanced production mix with around 65% oil and 35% gas after the completion of the transaction and the announced combination with BlueNord, with continued low operating costs of approximately $13 per boe and top quartile emission intensity at approximately 10-11 kg CO2 per boe. " This transaction strengthens our position as the largest independent E&P company in Europe. We are adding a significant portfolio of high-quality and long life assets, providing material cash flow generation and further strengthening our long term financial capacity and flexibility. With available liquidity of USD 7.5 billion and a reduced leverage ratio NIBD/EBITDAX of 0.3x at the end of the third quarter 2026, we can fully fund this transaction through existing liquidity while maintaining our leverage ratio significantly below our target of remaining below 1.3x through the cycles, also benefitting from the material cash generation in 2026 in the acquired business. " — Carlo Santopadre Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Vår Energi According to Vår Energi, the acquisition of ConocoPhillips’ Norwegian business and related UK infrastructure brings increased scale, operatorship, recovery potential, and value creation across the asset portfolio, with total reserves and resources to around 2.9 billion boe and reserves and resource life of approximately 14 years. This transaction is expected to deliver $700 million to $1 billion of synergies and additional value creation potential, net present value post-tax, alongside increased free cash flow generation and dividend capacity resulting in boosted dividend guidance for the fourth quarter of 2026 to $450 million. " The Greater Ekofisk Area is a world-class asset with significant remaining resources, extensive infrastructure and decades of production ahead. It remains one of the most important value creation hubs on the NCS. Supported by the highly competent and experienced organisation, which will be fully integrated into Vår Energi, we see substantial opportunities to increase recovery, mature additional resources, and create value over time. The transaction increases our long-term production target to above 500 kboepd into the mid-2030s, reinforcing our position as the Europe's largest independent E&P company and positioning Vår Energi among the world's leading offshore independents, while further strengthening our role as a reliable and secure supplier of energy to Europe. " — Walker added. Vår Energi sees significant opportunities to increase recovery and unlock additional value through an increased operated asset base, field developments, and continued development of resources across the portfolio. The company has strong available liquidity of $7.5 billion as on September 30, 2026. Advertisement " We remain firmly committed to a strong balance sheet and our investment grade credit rating. In consideration of the current volatile price environment, to further de-risk the acquisition we are establishing a commodity hedging programme related to the transaction volumes for 2027 through the first quarter 2028. As of today we have secured downside protection for approximately 80% of the additional gas volumes at approximately USD 110 per boe while retaining exposure to gas price upside. The transaction has an immediate positive effect on our free cash flow and dividend capacity, which is reflected in our increased fourth quarter 2026 dividend guidance of USD 450 million. " — Santopadre emphasized. The acquired portfolio comprises interests in 13 producing fields across the NCS, including the Greater Ekofisk Area, Troll , Heidrun , Alvheim , Oseberg , Visund , Aasta Hansteen , Grane , and Breidablikk , and related infrastructure. Vår Energi describes these assets as being low-cost and carrying limited near-term abandonment liabilities, with a balanced commodity mix and long reserve and resource life based on net 2P reserves of 414 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) and 2C resources of 101 million boe as of year-end 2025. The portfolio is perceived to complement the company’s existing asset base and increase its ownership in several core areas, with around 75% overlap on a combined 2P reserves basis, reflecting the strong strategic fit and existing knowledge of the assets. The transaction adds operatorship of the Greater Ekofisk Area, including Ekofisk, Eldfisk, Embla, Tor and Tommeliten Alfa and Gamma fields, as well as operatorship of the associated Norpipe pipeline and receiving Teesside facilities in the United Kingdom. Ekofisk was the first commercial discovery on the Norwegian Continental Shelf, and the Greater Ekofisk Area represents one of the largest oil and gas resource bases on the NCS, with initial oil in-place volumes estimated at around 10 billion boe. Vår Energi sees significant opportunities to increase recovery, mature additional resources and extend field life, unlocking long-term value creation. " Through the transaction, we are adding a highly complementary portfolio of long-life assets and a highly experienced and competent team. The increased scale across our operated portfolio creates significant opportunities for further value creation. By applying our value-driven operating model and project factory approach, we see significant potential to increase recovery, enhance performance and deliver substantial synergies across the combined portfolios. We also see opportunities to capture economies of scale across our supply chain and strategic partnerships, infrastructure, logistics and commercial activities. Together, this will strengthen our ability to grow the resource base, increase production and extend the lifetime of our assets in a value-accretive way. Yumna-2 came online in January 2021, while Yumna-3 began production in February 2021. The floating storage tanker was changed out in 2022 to allow for the tanker to be in the field for several years without the need for dry-docking. The mobile offshore production unit (MOPU) was also changed out with upgraded facilities the same year. articles.title: Mermaid reveals new framework targeting major savings on North Sea decom campaigns
articles.summary: Mermaid has unveiled a new North Sea decommissioning framework that could cut costs and execution time through shared campaigns.
articles.body: Business Developments & Projects November 23, 2026 · 1 minute ago Mermaid reveals new framework targeting major savings on North Sea decom campaigns Mermaid has unveiled a new North Sea decommissioning framework that could cut costs and execution time through shared campaigns. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Island Valiant Source: Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) Aberdeen-headquartered Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) has launched a new framework designed to curb the cost and duration of North Sea decommissioning, with modelling suggesting coordinated campaigns across four operators could enable savings of up to 45% and shorten execution time by 30%. Mermaid Subsea Services has revealed i-DECOM , a campaign framework that coordinates decommissioning across multiple North Sea operators, specifically designed to remove the cost and duplication that come with traditional project-by-project delivery. According to the company, modelling based on a shared campaign across four clients shows i-DECOM could reduce costs by 45% and execution time by 30% compared with standalone projects. " North Sea decommissioning takes more than putting a vessel on contract. It takes experience, technical understanding and the ability to match the right assets and equipment to the specific challenges of each scope. We’ve seen first-hand how poorly matched assets, repeated mobilisation and fragmented delivery drive up cost. So we start with the job: what exactly needs to be delivered, what the right technical solution is, and which assets are best suited to carry it out. Vessel utilisation matters, but it should never come before technical suitability or the client’s commercial interests. " — Scott Cormack Regional Director for Mermaid Subsea Services (UK) Related Articles Vessels North Sea quintet P&A ops done as Mermaid Subsea checks off decom mission 2 min read The UK player explains that decommissioning across the basin has traditionally been planned and contracted one project at a time, which leads to repeated vessel mobilizations, duplicated resources, and operational learning lost between campaigns. In a bid to tackle this, i-DECOM brings the work together, while each operator keeps control of its own scope and decisions, with the framework resting on what the firm describes as a simple principle, where the scope should determine the solution, not the other way round. Rather than planning work around the vessels available, Mermaid defines what each job requires, engineers the technical solution, and then selects the vessel and equipment to deliver it. i-DECOM is led by a specialist late-life team at the company’s Aberdeen facility. This latest development comes as Mermaid marks five years of operations in the North Sea. " i-DECOM applies that thinking at campaign level. By coordinating activity across operators, sharing resources and keeping a dedicated team of specialists together, we can cut unnecessary mobilisation and deliver meaningful savings, while operators keep control of their own scopes. It puts the operator’s objectives first: the right solution, using the right assets, at the right time. " — Cormack underlined. Reach the Offshore Energy industry in one go! (Source: Atomflot) Cargo volumes along Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) have surpassed 40 million tonnes for the first time, setting a new record for the Arctic shipping corridor. The milestone marks continued growth in Russian Arctic shipping, although volumes remain far below the ambitious targets set forth by President Vladimir Putin over the past decade. Rosatom chief executive Alexey Likhachev said cargo transportation crossed the 40-million-tonne threshold on November 17. The state nuclear corporation, which operates the route’s infrastructure, expects volumes to climb further before the end of the year. The previous record was 37.9 million tonnes in 2024. Traffic slipped to 37.02 million tonnes in 2025 , but the latest milestone puts the NSR back on an upward trajectory. Over the past five years, annual cargo volumes have increased from 34.87 million tonnes in 2021 to more than 40 million tonnes in 2026, an increase of roughly 15%. The route carried 34.07 million tonnes in 2022 and 36.25 million tonnes in 2023 before reaching its previous peak in 2024. The figures underline the NSR’s growing importance to Russia’s Arctic economy, but also show that recent growth has been relatively modest compared with the rapid expansion earlier in the decade. The latest record remains a long way from Moscow’s original ambitions. Putin set a target of 80 million tonnes of annual cargo traffic by 2024 in a 2018 presidential decree. Actual shipments that year reached less than half that volume. Even with this year’s record, the route is still operating at around half the level the Kremlin had targeted two years ago. Transit shipping, however, has shown stronger growth this year. Unlike total NSR cargo figures, which include shipments to and from Russian Arctic ports and resource projects, transit cargo refers to goods passing through the route between destinations outside the region connecting Europe and Asia. Transit volumes reached 6 million tonnes by early November, twice the level recorded during the same period last year, according to Russian Arctic Development Minister Alexey Chekunkov. Rosatom official Vladimir Panov has forecast that full-year transit traffic could exceed 7 million tonnes, which would more than double the 3.2 million tonnes recorded in 2025 . Independent tracking offers a more cautious picture. The Centre for High North Logistics estimated that transit cargo totaled approximately 3.7 million tonnes by the end of September, with the season potentially exceeding 4.5 million tonnes if ongoing voyages were completed . The final figures will help clarify how much of the Russian forecast materializes. The overall growth in NSR traffic remains heavily dependent on Russian energy exports, particularly liquefied natural gas, crude oil and petroleum products. Yamal LNG has been a major contributor, while new shipments from Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project could add further volumes in the coming years as its Arctic infrastructure develops. articles.summary: An Iranian oil tanker with no track record signaled earlier on Monday that it had sailed past a US blockade outside the Strait of Hormuz — an unlikely trajectory that is raising fresh questions about obfuscation tactics and analysts’ limited ability to accurately track movements in the area.

REUTERS/Amr Alfiky By Weilun Soon Nov 23, 2026 (Bloomberg) –An Iranian oil tanker with no track record signaled earlier on Monday that it had sailed past a US blockade outside the Strait of Hormuz — an unlikely trajectory that is raising fresh questions about obfuscation tactics and analysts’ limited ability to accurately track movements in the area. A vessel purporting to be the Khat Shekan, an Iranian very large crude carrier, appeared on Sunday on some ship-tracking platforms including MarineTraffic, indicating it was beginning an exit from the Persian Gulf. By Monday, signals suggested it had made it past US forces — a first since the blockade was reimposed in July. The catch is that the position is very likely fake and the ship — whose name translates as “Line Breaker” — may not exist at all, according to analysts and maritime tracking experts. Tehran may instead be sending a message on what it can still do to tangle the global oil trade after nine months of conflict with the US, by making already challenging monitoring efforts even more difficult, they said. “Any attempts to complicate the monitoring of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz are an unwelcome addition to an already dangerous situation,” said Mark Douglas, an analyst at ship-tracking platform Starboard Maritime Intelligence. The signals suggest the vessel is a laden crude tanker heading for China’s Zhoushan port, but it has no International Maritime Organization number, a unique identifier for vessels that remains through their operational life. A search done on its maritime mobile service identity, or MMSI number on the IMO database, yields no results, with an error message stating: “Only ships in service are displayed.” There is also no record of voyages prior to Sunday, and the vessel does not appear on Bloomberg or other ship-tracking and intelligence platforms, including Starboard, Kpler, Vortexa and Equasis. “Our analysis indicates AIS spoofing,” MarineTraffic wrote in a social media post , referring to the practice of sending false tracking or navigation data to plant incorrect information or confuse observers. Ship operators engaged in so-called “dark” trades have long sought to misrepresent vessels’ identities and locations in order to mask their journeys and the cargoes they are handling. Tankers ferrying US-sanctioned Iranian oil before the war often spoofed their positions, or assumed the identities of demolished ships. Iran all but closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to US attacks, but its crude exports continued in the first months of the conflict. The reintroduction of a US naval blockade, however, severed a vital financial lifeline for Tehran at a time when others in the Persian Gulf are using dark shuttles and other workarounds to restore pre-war flows. Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The country has repeatedly vowed to break the blockade, however. On Saturday, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the country would take “whatever measures are necessary” to do so. articles.summary: Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using naval drones on Sunday, the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

By Lina Golovnya Nov 23 (Reuters) – Ukraine sank a Russian naval corvette in a Libyan port using naval drones on Sunday , the day after a drone strike on a Russian military-linked cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Zelenskiy said on Monday morning that Ukraine used seven naval drones in Sunday’s attack, and had also hit the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara , which he said Russia had used to transport weapons. “Despite all the enemy’s attempts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette ‘ Mercury ‘ was sunk,” Zelenskiy posted on Telegram, the first official acknowledgement that Ukraine has carried out an attack in Libya. “We continue operations in designated waters.” Zelenskiy said a Russian Ka-27 combat helicopter had been destroyed along with the corvette. Russia’s Defence Ministry did not immediately comment. EASTERN LIBYA HAS MILITARY TIES TO RUSSIA After a civil war, eastern Libya is controlled by military commander Khalifa Haftar, whose Libyan National Army has ties with Russia, while the west is controlled by an internationally recognized Government of National Unity based in Tripoli. Libya’s eastern-based government said the corvette was docked at the Benghazi naval base on Sunday when it was hit. The Institute for the Study of War said it had stopped for several days, under a cooperation agreement, to refuel and resupply as it escorted Russian cargo ships that can carry military suppliesheading for Russia. Osama Hamad, prime minister of Libya’s eastern-based government, said he had asked the UN to investigate “suspicions that the boats had been launched from western Libya” and to verify the presence of Ukrainian military experts there. No comment was immediately available from the Tripoli government. Russia’s Transport Ministry said in March that Ukrainian naval drones launched from Libya had attacked the Arctic Metagaz, which was carrying liquefied natural gas from Murmansk. Libya’s maritime agency reported that the vessel had sunk between Libya and Malta after catching fire. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for that attack. GULF OF FINLAND DRONE ATTACK ON RUSSIAN SHIP On Saturday , a drone attack set fire to another Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, operated by the Russian defense logistics firm Oboronlogistika, in international waters in the Gulf of Finland. The Finnish military said it was likely to have been carried out by Ukraine, although Kyiv did not immediately comment. All 16 crew were evacuated onto a nearby Russian ship, one of them slightly injured. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov responded to a question about the attack by saying there was a “dangerous trend of increasing terrorist activity” in the Baltic Sea. He said Moscow hoped states in the area would warn Kyiv off such operations. Russian, Estonian and Finnish vessels fought the fire after the Sparta II drifted into Finnish waters, and a Russian ship began towing it away on Sunday. US-backed talks between Russia and Ukraine resumed this month after a nine-month hiatus in an effort to end the war, Europe’s biggest since World War Two, albeit with little result so far. Mykola Bielieskov of the National Institute for Strategic Studies in Kyiv said Ukraine was looking to strengthen its position with “horizontal escalation.” “Since neither side is able to compel the other to accept terms of settlement through the battlefield only, both try to find new ways to pressure each other,” he said. articles.body: Asia Dry Cargo Precious Shipping secures year-long ultramax charter Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 763 1 minute read Precious Shipping Precious Shipping Thailand’s Precious Shipping has secured another index-linked ultramax charter with Singapore’s PACC Line, fixing the 2015-built Sarita Naree for up to 13 months at a current equivalent rate of around $23,700 per day. The Khalid Hashim-led owner said the 62,964 dwt vessel started an 11-to-13-month charter on November 22 at a gross variable rate equivalent to 103% of the Baltic Exchange Supramax Index (BSI-63K) weighted time-charter average over the preceding 15 days. The hire will fluctuate with the index rather than remain fixed at the current level. The latest agreement follows a similar fixture in September, when Precious chartered its 2016-built ultramax Sunisa Naree to PACC Line for 11 to 13 months at the same 103% index-linked rate, then equivalent to about $23,000 per day. Both vessels were built at China’s Taizhou Sanfu Ship Engineering, a yard that has become central to Precious Shipping’s fleet renewal programme. PACC Line, part of the Kuok Maritime Group through Pacific Carriers, operates a fleet of around 50 vessels across dry bulk, breakbulk and project cargo trades. The latest fixing adds to a string of longer-term employment deals for Precious. In October, the company chartered its recently delivered Rossarin Naree to Oman’s Asyad Shipping for 12 to 14 months at 108% of the same index, then equivalent to about $24,000 per day. Precious has also continued investing in larger bulkers, returning to Sanfu in September for four 64,500 dwt ultramaxes worth $141.8m, with deliveries scheduled between April 2030 and January 2031. articles.body: Asia Europe Offshore Renewables Kansai Electric takes 40% stake in Polish offshore wind project Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 549 1 minute read Ocean Winds Ocean Winds Japan’s Kansai Electric Power has agreed to acquire a 40% interest in Ocean Winds’ 390 MW BC-Wind offshore wind development in Poland, marking its first investment in the country. The Japanese utility signed a share purchase agreement with Ocean Winds on November 19, and the transaction will be carried out through its wholly owned subsidiary, KPIC Netherlands. Kansai will acquire its interest in C-Wind Polska, the project company developing the wind farm, leaving Ocean Winds with a 60% holding following completion. BC-Wind is located approximately 23 km off Poland’s Baltic Sea coast and will comprise 26 Siemens Gamesa turbines with a maximum output of 15 MW each. The project is expected to start generating electricity in 2028 and can supply around 500,000 Polish households. Ocean Winds, a joint venture between EDP Renewables and Engie, reached financial close on BC-Wind in December 2025, securing approximately €2bn ($2.2bn) in project financing. Offshore construction is advancing, with foundation installation scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. Belgian contractor DEME has secured the foundation and subsea cable installation work, while Seaway 7 is responsible for installing the transition piece and offshore substation. Cadeler will handle the transportation and installation of the 26 turbines in 2028. Kansai said the acquisition would increase the attributable capacity of its overseas power generation portfolio to approximately 2.65 GW once completed. The deal expands Japanese investment in Poland’s offshore wind sector as the country moves ahead with its first generation of large-scale Baltic Sea projects. articles.title: €2.8 billion UK-Germany energy link continues to take shape as nearshore cabling works begin on German coast
articles.summary: Prysmian has started laying 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling at Wilhelmshaven, advancing the 725-kilometer UK-Germany electricity interconnector.
articles.body: Business Developments & Projects November 23, 2026 · 29 minutes ago €2.8 billion UK-Germany energy link continues to take shape as nearshore cabling works begin on German coast Prysmian has started laying 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling at Wilhelmshaven, advancing the 725-kilometer UK-Germany electricity interconnector. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Prysmian's Ulisse cable laying vessel Source: NeuConnect A new milestone in bringing the first direct electricity connection between the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany closer to reality has been reached, with cable installation works advancing along Germany’s northern coast near Wilhelmshaven. A cable-laying vessel operated by Italy’s Prysmian has embarked on the installation of 30 kilometers of nearshore cabling, marking further progress in establishing the electricity link between the two countries. Prysmian’s Ulisse cable laying vessel has begun laying 30 kilometers of cabling at the German shore in Wilhelmshaven for NeuConnect , described as the first direct energy link between the UK and Germany, following the continued progress of the wider 700-kilometer subsea cabling program, which passed the halfway stage earlier this year. The Italian contractor kicked off NeuConnect ’s subsea cabling works at the end of 2024, with all cabling completed in UK waters earlier this year and now continuing in German waters. Alongside this, cable landing works have started at the German end of the cabling route, including the Ulisse vessel’s laying of 30 kilometers of cabling in the near shore area in northern Germany. Upon completion of cable landing works, the offshore cable will reach the mainland at Hooksiel, where a 12-kilometer onshore section of cabling is in place to connect into NeuConnect’s new converter station currently under construction near Wilhelmshaven. NeuConnect is expected to be one of the world’s largest interconnectors with around 725 kilometers of land and subsea cables forming an invisible energy highway to connect two of Europe’s largest energy markets for the first time. articles.body: Dry Cargo Greater China Jinhui finds new buyer for supramax at higher price Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 677 1 minute read Jinhui Holdings Jinhui Holdings Hong Kong-based dry bulk owner Jinhui Shipping and Transportation has found a new buyer for its 2012-built supramax Jin Bi , securing $17.8m for a vessel it unsuccessfully tried to sell for $14.4m earlier this year. The Oslo-listed company has signed a memorandum of agreement with Singapore-based Global Pacific Shipping for the 56,361 dwt bulker, with delivery scheduled between November 25 and December 30. The deal marks a second attempt to sell the ship after a previous agreement with Hong Kong’s Xing Le Investments collapsed in January. Jinhui had agreed to sell Jin Bi for $14.4m in December 2025, but the transaction was cancelled the following month after a contractual condition relating to timely delivery could not be met. The latest agreement puts another $3.4m on the price tag and comes with improved payment terms. Unlike the previous arrangement, which included $7m payable over four years, Global Pacific will pay the full purchase price before delivery. Jinhui said it expects to book a gain of approximately $5.2m on the sale, based on the vessel’s carrying value of $12.6m at the end of September. Proceeds will be used primarily to repay short-term borrowings, settle outstanding liabilities and strengthen liquidity. The disposal adds to Jinhui’s ongoing fleet reshuffle. Last month, the company agreed to sell the 2007-built, 55,496 dwt Jin Xing for $14.6m, continuing its clearout of older supramax tonnage. At the same time, the Ng family-controlled owner has been investing heavily in larger bulk carriers, with 14 ultramax newbuildings lined up at Chinese yards, including Jiangmen Nanyang, New Dayang and Jiangsu Hantong. Jinhui currently operates 19 bulk carriers, comprising 16 owned vessels and three chartered-in ships, ahead of the latest disposal. articles.body: Middle East Offshore Arabian Drilling picks up $400m in long-term offshore work Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 1,216 1 minute read Arabian Drilling Arabian Drilling Saudi Arabian drilling contractor Arabian Drilling has secured a SAR1.5bn ($400m) long-term contract from Khafji Joint Operations (KJO) to provide and operate two self-propelled offshore service units. The agreement replaces existing contracts covering two offshore service units operating for KJO. The first unit will operate under a 10-year contract, with work expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026. The second has secured a 15-year agreement, with operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2028. Arabian Drilling said the agreements represent the longest offshore service unit contracts in its history and will provide additional long-term revenue visibility. The latest award takes the company’s cumulative contracted backlog to approximately SAR18.5bn ($4.9bn), a record for the Saudi contractor. Khafji Joint Operations is a joint venture between Aramco Gulf Operations and Kuwait Gulf Oil, responsible for oil and gas production in the Saudi–Kuwaiti Divided Zone. The contract follows Arabian Drilling’s September award of four high-specification offshore jackup contracts from KJO, worth approximately SAR2bn ($533m). Those four-year drilling contracts are expected to contribute to revenue from the final quarter of 2026. Arabian Drilling said the latest agreement maintains its entire share of KJO’s offshore service unit segment. The company did not disclose the names of the two units or the individual contract values. articles.summary: State-owned Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is pressing ahead with a fleet expansion drive worth an estimated $3.2bn, launching tenders for up to 22 newbuildings across the gas carrier, tanker and container segments, alongside a separate push for secondhand tonnage. articles.body: Asia Containers Gas Tankers Shipping Corp of India casts $3.2bn net for 22 ships Adis Ajdin November 23, 2026 0 3,563 2 minutes read SCI SCI State-owned Shipping Corporation of India (SCI) is pressing ahead with a fleet expansion drive worth an estimated $3.2bn, launching tenders for up to 22 newbuildings across the gas carrier, tanker and container segments, alongside a separate push for secondhand tonnage. The Mumbai-listed owner has issued tenders covering eight 88,000 cu m very large gas carriers (VLGCs), six 18,000 teu containerships, up to six 8,000 teu boxships and two 155,000 dwt suezmax tankers. The largest package involves eight VLGCs, with bids due by January 27, 2027, and an estimated combined value of $950m. The vessels are being sought for a proposed joint venture involving state-owned energy companies Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum. The gas carrier programme comes with a significant domestic construction requirement. Two vessels are to be built at an established overseas yard, with the remaining six earmarked for construction in India under arrangements involving qualified international shipbuilders. SCI is taking a similar approach to its six 18,000 teu containerships. Two vessels are intended for its own fleet, while four are earmarked for the proposed Bharat Container Shipping Line, part of India’s efforts to expand its presence in international container shipping. The tender again splits construction between two ships overseas and four in India, with bids due by December 10.The company is also pursuing six LNG-ready containerships of 8,000 teu, comprising two firm vessels and four options, in a programme previously valued at around $720m. That tender, first launched in July, has since been revised to require two vessels to be constructed overseas and four in India if the full package proceeds. Bids are now due by December 7. In the tanker segment, SCI has opened bidding for two 155,000 dwt suezmax crude carriers, with offers due by December 10. The owner is also looking to the secondhand market to bolster its container fleet. A separate tender seeks two firm and two optional boxships of between 1,500 teu and 2,500 teu, with vessels up to 20 years old eligible. The deadline for offers is December 17. The latest procurement drive represents a major expansion of SCI’s fleet renewal ambitions, with the government using state-backed orders to attract foreign shipbuilding expertise and move more complex vessel construction to Indian yards. SCI currently operates a fleet of 58 vessels across the tanker, dry bulk, container and offshore sectors, according to its latest published fleet figures. Just two are owned containerships. None of the newbuilding packages has yet been announced as a firm shipbuilding contract. The $3.2bn figure represents an industry estimate of the proposed programme, which includes optional tonnage. articles.summary: US energy major ExxonMobil and its partners have taken a final investment decision worth an estimated $4bn to redevelop the Kizomba A and B fields offshore Angola, while announcing a fresh hydrocarbon discovery in the same block. articles.body: Africa Americas Offshore ExxonMobil greenlights $4bn Angola offshore redevelopment Bojan Lepic November 23, 2026 0 1,377 1 minute read ExxonMobil ExxonMobil US energy major ExxonMobil and its partners have taken a final investment decision worth an estimated $4bn to redevelop the Kizomba A and B fields offshore Angola, while announcing a fresh hydrocarbon discovery in the same block. The investment decision, formalised on November 19, completes the approvals for the Block 15 Life Extension Project, following the sanctioning of the Kizomba C redevelopment last year. The programme will make use of existing offshore infrastructure to develop additional resources across the Kizomba production hub, located around 145 km off Angola’s northern coast. The investment also includes plans to develop the Likembe field, with ExxonMobil looking to extend production from one of Angola’s most prolific deepwater areas. The Block 15 production-sharing agreement was previously extended until 2037, giving the partners more time to develop remaining resources. Meanwhile, Angola’s National Oil, Gas and Biofuels Agency (ANPG) confirmed a new discovery at the Tchihumba West-01ST1 exploration well, approximately 350 km northwest of Luanda. The Valaris DS-9 drillship drilled the well in about 1,400 m of water and encountered 65.4 m of hydrocarbon-bearing sandstone with good reservoir characteristics. The discovery is the 21st recorded in Block 15 and the second this year. No recoverable resource estimate has been disclosed. ExxonMobil operates Block 15 with a 36% stake, alongside Azule Energy entities holding a combined 42%, Equinor with 12%, and Sonangol with 10%. The latest investment and exploration success comes as Angola seeks to sustain offshore production by redeveloping mature fields and pursuing further deepwater exploration.
